dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:3801.text: Fetters and handcuffs. Formed from 木, with 戒 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a general name for implements. Another: to hold. Another: one that contains something is 械; one that does not is 器.

shuowen:3802.text: Restraints. Formed from 木 and 手; 手 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:3803.text: Foot fetters. Formed from 木, with 至 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3804.text: Hand restraints. Formed from 木, with 告 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3805.text: 櫪㯕, defined as 椑指; the object is uncertain. Formed from 木, with 歴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3806.text: 櫪㯕; the object is uncertain. Formed from 木, with 斯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3807.text: A cage, 櫳. Formed from 木, with 監 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a pen.

shuowen:3808.text: A cage, 檻. Formed from 木, with 龍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3809.text: A cage for keeping tigers and rhinoceroses. Formed from 木, with 甲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3810.text: To enclose: something used to cover a corpse. Formed from 木, with 官 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3811.text: A coffin. Formed from 木, with 親 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “The soldiers carry coffins.”

shuowen:3812.text: A coffin box. Formed from 木, with 彗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3813.text: A wooden enclosure around a burial. Formed from 木, with 𩫏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3814.text: A raised marker, 楬桀. Formed from 木, with 曷 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Set up a marker and write upon it.”

shuowen:3815.text: An unfilial bird. At the solstice owls are caught and dismembered. Formed from a bird’s head above 木.

shuowen:3816.text: To assist. Formed from 木, with 非 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3817.text: A tree whose fruit can be used as dye. Formed from 木, with 巵 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3818.text: A terrace with a roof. Formed from 木, with 䠶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3819.text: A spear. Formed from 木, with 朔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3820.text: A clothes rack. Formed from 木, with 施 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3821.text: A couch. Formed from 木, with 𦐇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3822.text: A supporting base, 柎. Formed from 木, with 質 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3823.text: Something used to propel a boat. Formed from 木, with 翟 indicating the sound; some forms use 卓. The Records of the Historian also uses 濯 for it.

shuowen:3824.text: 桔槹, a water-lifting device. Formed from 木, with 臯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3825.text: A peg or stake. Formed from 木, with 舂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3826.text: A fruit. Formed from 木, with 嬰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3827.text: The 桋 tree. Formed from 木, with abbreviated 策 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3828.text: To move. Formed from 木. Guan Pu explains it as 日 inside 木. All characters in this group follow 東.

shuowen:3829.text: Two 東 elements; 曹 follows this. Further explanation is missing.

shuowen:3830.text: A cluster of trees on level ground is called 林. Formed from two 木. All characters in this group follow 林.

shuowen:3831.text: Abundant. Formed from 林 and 𡘲. Some explain it as the graph for 規模, “scale”: formed from 大 and 𠦜, an accumulation in number; 林 means many trees. 𠦜 uses the same principle as 庶. The Book of Shang says: “The many grasses flourish abundantly.” The analysis is uncertain.

shuowen:3832.text: Trees growing densely together. Formed from 林, with abbreviated 𩰪 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3833.text: Clustered shrubs, also called 荊. Formed from 林, with 疋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3834.text: The lush, trailing appearance of branches, 棽儷. Formed from 林, with 今 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3835.text: Trees flourishing. Formed from 林, with 矛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3836.text: An official guarding mountain forests. Formed from 林, with 鹿 indicating the sound. Another explanation: woods adjoining a mountain are 麓. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Shalu collapsed.”

shuowen:3837.text: The ridge beam of a building with multiple roofs. Formed from 林, with 分 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3838.text: The appearance of many trees. Formed from 林 and 木. Read like 參 in 曾參.

shuowen:3839.text: Found in Buddhist writings from the Western Regions; its meaning has not been ascertained.

shuowen:3840.text: The first emergence of plants. Formed from 丨 piercing 一 upward, about to produce branches and leaves; 一 is the ground. All characters in this group follow 才.

shuowen:3841.text: When the sun first emerges from Tang Valley in the east, the 榑桑 on which it rises is the 叒 tree. Pictographic. All characters in this group follow 叒.

shuowen:3842.text: The tree whose leaves silkworms eat. Formed from 叒 and 木.

shuowen:3843.text: To emerge. Depicts grass growing beyond 屮, its branches and stems enlarging and extending somewhere. 一 is the ground. All characters in this group follow 之.

shuowen:3844.text: Plants growing unchecked. Formed from 之 above 土. Read like 皇.

shuowen:3845.text: To encircle. Formed from reversed 之, going all around. All characters in this group follow 帀. This is Zhou Sheng’s explanation.

shuowen:3846.text: Two thousand five hundred men make a 師. Formed from 帀 and 𠂤; 𠂤, surrounded on four sides, conveys a multitude.

shuowen:3847.text: To advance. Depicts plants growing ever more luxuriantly and emerging upward. All characters in this group follow 出.

shuowen:3848.text: To roam. Formed from 出 and 放.

shuowen:3849.text: To put goods out for sale. Formed from 出 and 買.

shuowen:3850.text: To release grain for sale. Formed from 出 and 䊮; 䊮 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:3851.text: 𣙗𦤙, uneasy. Formed from 出, with 臬 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “𣙗𦤙.”

shuowen:3852.text: Plants flourishing, 𣎵𣎵. Pictographic, with 八 indicating the sound. All characters in this group follow 𣎵. Read like 輩.

shuowen:3853.text: The flourishing appearance of plants, 𢍚孛. Formed from 𣎵, with 𢌿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3854.text: Plants having stems and leaves that can be made into ropes. Formed from 𣎵 and 糸. Du Lin says 𣎵 is also the graph for the 朱 tree.

shuowen:3855.text: Luxuriant, 𢍚, hence formed from 𣎵; also a person’s complexion, hence 子. The Analects says: “His complexion suddenly changed.”

shuowen:3856.text: To stop. Formed from flourishing 𣎵, with one horizontal stroke stopping it.

shuowen:3857.text: Plants reaching the south have branches capable of bearing growth. Formed from 𣎵, with 𢆉 indicating the sound; the wording 枝任 is uncertain.

shuowen:3858.text: To advance. Depicts plants growing out above the soil. All characters in this group follow 生.

shuowen:3859.text: Plants flourishing, 𡴀𡴀. Formed from 生, extending both upward and downward.

shuowen:3860.text: To give birth or produce. Formed from 生, with abbreviated 彥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3861.text: Abundant and large. Formed from 生, with 降 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3862.text: Plants bearing fruit luxuriantly, 甤甤. Formed from 生, with abbreviated 豨 indicating the sound. Read like 綏.

shuowen:3863.text: The appearance of many living things standing together. Formed from two 生. The Odes says: “The deer stand in multitudes.”

shuowen:3864.text: A plant leaf. Formed from a drooping ear, piercing 一 above, with roots below. Pictographic. All characters in this group follow 乇.

shuowen:3865.text: The drooping flowers and leaves of plants. Pictographic. All characters in this group follow 𠂹.

shuowen:3866.text: The flowers of plants. Formed from 𠂹, with 亏 indicating the sound. All characters in this group follow 𠌶.

shuowen:3867.text: Flourishing. Formed from 𠌶, with 韋 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Do not the calyxes flourish?”

shuowen:3868.text: Blossoming. Formed from 艸 and 𠌶. All characters in this group follow 華.

shuowen:3869.text: The white flowers of plants. Formed from 華 and 白.

shuowen:3870.text: The bent top of a tree, stopped and unable to rise further. All characters in this group follow 𥝌.

shuowen:3871.text: To stop over many petty considerations. Formed from 𥝌 and 支, with 只 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a tree.

shuowen:3872.text: 䅩䅓, hesitant and stopping. Formed from 𥝌 and 又, with 句 indicating the sound; 又 is abbreviated 丑. Another explanation: a tree name.

shuowen:3873.text: To remain and stop. Formed from 𥝌 and 尤, with 旨 indicating the sound. All characters in this group follow 稽.

shuowen:3874.text: To stop firmly. Formed from abbreviated 稽, with 卓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3875.text: To stop hesitantly, 𥢑䅓. Formed from abbreviated 稽, with 咎 indicating the sound. Read like 皓. Attendant Jia says 稽, 𥢔 and 𥢑 are all tree names.

shuowen:3876.text: A bird’s dwelling in a tree is 巢; in a hole, 窠. Formed from 木; pictographic. All characters in this group follow 巢.

shuowen:3877.text: To overturn. Formed from 寸, with 𦥑 overturning it; 寸 represents a human hand. It uses abbreviated 巢. Du Lin regards it as 貶 in 貶損, “to diminish.”

shuowen:3878.text: Tree sap, usable for coating objects. Pictographic: lacquer drips down like water. All characters in this group follow 桼.

shuowen:3879.text: To lacquer. Formed from 桼, with 髟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3880.text: After applying a lacquer-and-powder coating, to lacquer again. Formed from 桼, with 包 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3881.text: To bind. Formed from 囗 and 木. All characters in this group follow 束.

shuowen:3882.text: To distinguish and select. Formed from 束 and 八; 八 means dividing.

shuowen:3883.text: A small bundle. Formed from 束, with 幵 indicating the sound. Read like 繭.

shuowen:3884.text: To oppose or go against. Formed from 束 and 刀; 刀 cuts it apart.

shuowen:3885.text: A sack. Formed from 束, with 圂 indicating the sound. All characters in this group follow 㯻.

shuowen:3886.text: A bag. Formed from abbreviated 㯻, with 石 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3887.text: A sack. Formed from abbreviated 㯻, with abbreviated 襄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3888.text: A large sack on a cart. Formed from abbreviated 㯻, with 咎 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Stowing bows and arrows in their cases.”

shuowen:3889.text: The swollen appearance of a bag. Formed from abbreviated 㯻, with abbreviated 匋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3890.text: To surround. Depicts encircling. All characters in this group follow 囗.

shuowen:3891.text: The form of Heaven. Formed from 囗, with 瞏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3892.text: Round. Formed from 囗, with 專 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3893.text: A compass or circle. Formed from 囗, with 肙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3894.text: To turn around. Formed from 囗, with 云 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3895.text: Completely round. Formed from 囗, with 員 indicating the sound. Read like 員.

shuowen:3896.text: To turn. Formed from 囗, with the middle depicting turning around.

shuowen:3897.text: To draw up plans for difficulties. Formed from 囗 and 啚; 啚 conveys difficulty.

shuowen:3898.text: To move in a circle. Formed from 囗, with 睪 indicating the sound. The Book of Documents says: “Called 圛.” 圛 means rising clouds, partly present and partly absent. Read like 驛.

shuowen:3899.text: A state. Formed from 囗 and 或.

shuowen:3900.text: A passage within a palace. Formed from 囗, depicting palace walls, a passage and the part above. The Odes says: “The inner passage of the household.”
